fullText:
Genesis Tech kept charging customers after confirming cancellation, the FTC alleges—leaving people paying after they thought they were out.

The FTC says the enterprise behind MadMuscles, Harna and Unimeal advertised free or low, one-time prices while burying recurring charges in small print. Cancellation options were missing, customers had to explain why they wanted to leave, and some faced duplicate charges or unwanted add-ons. Separately, Noom customers challenged automatic enrollment in multi-month plans and difficult trial cancellations.

The receipts: The FTC’s June 17, 2026 announcement described a temporary court halt—not a final ruling on its Genesis Tech allegations. Noom’s settlement received final approval in July 2022: $56 million plus $6 million in subscription fee credits. People v. Beachbody, LLC, Final Judgment, ¶¶7(c), 7(f)(4): separate consent to recurring terms; cancellation effective upon request, subject to reasonable confirmation. Beachbody admitted no wrongdoing.

Follow the cancellation instructions. Save your request, confirmation and chats with dates. Check subsequent bank and card statements. If charges continue, dispute them with your card issuer and follow up in writing. A cancellation confirmation is evidence—not the end of checking.
